openers.hook_source: list trigger (opened a new location this year (from the list)) and the notes: one calendar across locations raised in 4 of 7 clinic calls

lines.line: This is Dana with Example Booking Software.
Your clinic is on a list of practices that opened a new site this year. When we talk to clinics with more than one site, four in seven bring up keeping one schedule across offices.
Which system do your front desks book into today?

openers.for: Owner, salon group with 2 to 4 locations
openers.hook_source: list trigger (takes bookings by phone and direct message only (from the list)) and the notes: deposits chased by hand raised in 5 of 5 salon calls

lines.line: This is Dana with Example Booking Software.
Your salons take bookings by phone and message. Of the salon owners we spoke to this quarter, five of five said they chase deposits by hand.
When someone books a long colour, how do you take the deposit today?

openers.for: Either persona, when the list gives no trigger
openers.hook_source: the notes: no-shows raised in 7 of 12 calls, the most of any pain

lines.line: This is Dana with Example Booking Software.
We call clinics and salons with more than one location, and no-shows came up in seven of our last twelve calls.
Roughly how many appointments a month end up as no-shows for you?

meeting_ask.line: Then let's put half an hour in the diary with whoever runs the other desks. I can do Tuesday at 2 or Wednesday at 9; which suits you?

branches.they_say: We're on a scheduler already, it came with the practice software.
branches.label: already use a booking tool
branches.what_sits_behind_it: In the notes it is often a scheduler bundled with practice or EHR software, so nobody picked it for booking.

reply.line: Good to know, which one is it? The thing we look at is whether a desk at one office can fill a gap at another.

branches.goes_to: log current_tool; if they can't fill gaps across sites, go to the meeting ask

branches.label: staff won't learn a new system
branches.what_sits_behind_it: The owner worries about team pushback more than the tool.

reply.line: Fair worry. If your stylists only had to check one screen on their phone, which part of the day would it change for them?

branches.goes_to: ask for the meeting with the owner and one stylist

branches.label: send me an email
branches.what_sits_behind_it: Often a polite exit; sometimes a real preference.

reply.line: Sure, I'll send it while we're talking. What's the best address, and is there someone at the other sites I should copy?

branches.goes_to: log decision_maker if they name someone; the email carries two times for the discovery call

branches.they_say: My clients like to call, they're older.
branches.label: clients prefer to phone
branches.what_sits_behind_it: The owner fears losing older clients who call.

reply.line: Phone bookings still work; the front desk books into the same calendar. Roughly how many calls a day are just to confirm or move a time?

branches.they_say: Moving all our patients over sounds like a nightmare.
branches.label: data migration worry
branches.what_sits_behind_it: Fear of losing history and a messy switch.

reply.line: That's the part we do for you: we move the existing appointments over. What would you need to see to trust that?

branches.goes_to: ask for the meeting, with the person who owns the patient records

branches.they_say: Everything charges us per site, it adds up.
branches.label: price per location
branches.what_sits_behind_it: They've been burned by tools that bill per site.

reply.line: Good question. Our Business plan is priced by bookable staff, not by location. How many people take bookings across your sites?

branches.goes_to: fill locations_staff, then ask for the meeting

watch_list.label: contract renews later
watch_list.why_no_branch: heard once; write a branch if it comes up again

cold_call_guide.say_once_rule: Each branch reply is said once. A second identical objection: offer the email or close, then log the label and the outcome so the recount shows which replies turn into meetings. Asked not to be called: confirm the number comes off the list, and take it off.

gatekeeper.why: At clinics and salons the person who answers usually runs the front desk, so they know the current setup. Ask them one field question, then who decides and when that person is in.

line.line: This is Dana with Example Booking Software. Quick one for you: which system do you book patients into at the front desk? And who decides on that system, and when are they usually in?

voicemails.line: This is Dana with Example Booking Software, for the practice manager. A three-site physio clinic we work with went from eleven percent no-shows to six in ninety days. I'm emailing you how they set it up this afternoon, from Example Booking Software.

calling_rules: Check Do Not Call lists and local calling hours.
US: the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule bans misrepresentations on B2B calls since 2024; every claim here has a source in the brief.
The FCC treats AI-generated voices as artificial under the TCPA (2024); these guides are for a person to say.
Recording consent follows the law where each person on the call was; this call was recorded with consent.
what_would_make_it_better: 1 reply was heard once (contract renews later); log 10 more calls and recount.
Add a salon customer result so the salon demo gets a proof section.
Connect CallRail if calls are recorded there, so reviews pull the transcript directly.
